e.etymology: A Biblical name, a form of Jaaziel, a Levite musician in 1 Chronicles who is also called Aziel. In the US it is used mainly by Spanish-speaking families.

e.meaning: short form of Helena or Magdalena
e.etymology: A German, Scandinavian and Russian pet form of Helena, Magdalena and Yelena, now used as a name in its own right.
namesakes: Lena Headey (Cersei in Game of Thrones)

assoc.t: Lena River in Siberia

e.meaning: little poet (Irish); or darling, fair (Welsh Tegan)
e.etymology: For boys, from an Irish surname based on a pet form of Tadhg, poet. For girls, a variant of Tegan, from Welsh tegan, pet or darling.
The feminine form of Daniel, from Hebrew Daniyyel, God is my judge, the name of the prophet who survives the lions' den.
From Italian Ofelia, coined by the poet Jacopo Sannazaro in 1504, probably from Greek opheleia, help. Shakespeare gave it to the ill-fated young woman who loves Hamlet.

assoc.t: Hamlet's doomed love in Shakespeare's Hamlet
Ophelia, 2016 hit song by the Lumineers
The Fate of Ophelia, 2025 Taylor Swift single

e.note: Shakespeare's Ophelia goes mad and drowns, a tragic story that people who know Hamlet will bring up.

e.meaning: short form of Gianna (God is gracious) or Georgia
e.etymology: From Italian Gia, a short form of Gianna and Giovanna, feminine forms of John. In English it is also a clipping of Georgia.

assoc.t: Gia, 1998 HBO film starring Angelina Jolie

e.etymology: From German Otto, a short form of old Germanic names beginning with aud, wealth, the same element as Ed- in Edward and Edmund. Four Holy Roman Emperors bore it.
namesakes: Otto von Bismarck (first chancellor of Germany)

assoc.t: Otto, the school bus driver on The Simpsons
A Man Called Otto, 2022 Tom Hanks film

e.etymology: From an English surname and place name, Old English claeg, clay, plus tun, settlement: a town on clay soil.

assoc.t: Clayton Homes, maker of manufactured houses

e.etymology: A recent American name that pairs Mila with the -lani ending of Hawaiian names such as Leilani and Kailani. Milani is also an Italian surname meaning from Milan.

assoc.t: Milani Cosmetics drugstore makeup

e.etymology: A respelling of Cattleya, an orchid genus named for the English botanist William Cattley. Zoe Saldana's character Cataleya in the 2011 film Colombiana launched it as a given name.

assoc.t: Cataleya, Zoe Saldana's assassin in Colombiana

e.etymology: From Arabic ali, high or exalted. Ali ibn Abi Talib was the cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the fourth caliph. In English Ali is also a nickname for Alison and Alistair.

assoc.t: Muhammad Ali, heavyweight boxing champion

e.etymology: The feminine form of Church Latin Angelus, from Greek angelos, messenger or angel. It was a top-ten US girls' name from 1965 to 1979.
namesakes: Angela Lansbury (star of Murder, She Wrote)

e.etymology: A pet form of Eva, Eve, Evelyn and Evangeline with the -ie ending, now given as a name in its own right.

assoc.t: sounds like Eevee, the fox-like Pokémon

e.etymology: The English form of Irish Aodhán, a diminutive of Aodh, fire, the name of a Celtic sun god. Saint Aidan founded the monastery of Lindisfarne in the 7th century.
namesakes: Aidan Shaw (Sex and the City character)

e.etymology: A modern American name of uncertain origin. It shares its sound with Amari, Jamari and Omari, and is often linked to the Arabic word qamar, moon.
The feminine form of the Roman family name Octavius, from octavus, eighth. Octavia was the sister of the emperor Augustus and the wife of Mark Antony.
namesakes: Octavia E. Butler (science fiction author of Kindred)

e.etymology: From an Irish surname, an anglicized form of O Cuidighthigh, descendant of the helpful one, and of Mac Oda, son of Odo. Buffalo Bill Cody gave it a Wild West flavor.

assoc.t: Cody, Wyoming, rodeo town near Yellowstone

e.etymology: From a Scottish and northern English surname, a nickname for someone with red hair or a ruddy face, from the old northern form of the word red.
An American coinage, a variant of Jalen. Jalen spread from basketball player Jalen Rose, born in 1973, whose mother formed it from the names James and Leonard.
From French Adélaïde, from Old High German Adalheid, noble plus kind or nature; Alice and Heidi come from the same name. Queen Adelaide, wife of William IV, gave her name to the Australian city.

assoc.t: Adelaide, capital of South Australia

e.meaning: dew of God (Hebrew); also a form of Thalia, to flourish
e.etymology: A modern Hebrew name read as tal, dew, plus a short form of the name of God. It is also a spelling of Thalia, from Greek thallo, to flourish, and a short form of Natalia.
namesakes: Talia Shire (Adrian in the Rocky films)

e.etymology: The Spanish and Portuguese form of Francis, from Latin Franciscus, Frenchman. It spread in honor of Saint Francis of Assisi, whose father gave him the nickname.
From an English surname and place name, Old English hara, hare, or haer, rock, plus leah, wood or clearing.

assoc.t: Harley-Davidson motorcycles, known as Harleys
Harley Quinn, DC Comics antiheroine

e.meaning: warrior, brave; also the koa tree
e.etymology: From Hawaiian koa, which means warrior or courage and also names the koa, a large native hardwood tree. It is also a short form of longer Hawaiian names containing koa.

assoc.t: KOA, Kampgrounds of America campground chain
koa wood, Hawaiian hardwood used for ukuleles

e.etymology: From Sanskrit Kali, the name of the Hindu goddess of time, death and change, from kala, black or time. In the US it also serves as a spelling of Callie.

assoc.t: fierce Hindu goddess of time and destruction
Kali Linux, a security-testing operating system

e.note: Kali is a major and fearsome Hindu goddess; the name also sounds like Cali, slang for California.

e.etymology: From French Céline, from the Latin name Caelina, built on caelum, heaven. It is also a French short form of Marceline.
namesakes: Celine Dion (Canadian singer of My Heart Will Go On)

assoc.t: singer Celine Dion
Celine, French luxury fashion house

e.etymology: A spelling of Brian, the Irish name made famous by the high king Brian Boru, who died in 1014. It probably comes from an old Celtic word for a hill or for something high.
The Spanish form of Joshua, Josué, from Latin Iosue and Hebrew Yehoshua, Yahweh is salvation. In the Bible Joshua leads the Israelites into Canaan after Moses.
A short form of Nikolas, Nikola and Nikolaos, from Greek nike, victory, and laos, people. It is a given name in its own right in Finland and the Balkans.
A spelling of the English surname Sidney, from Old English words for a wide meadow by a river. The Australian city was named in 1788 for Lord Sydney, a British home secretary.

assoc.t: largest city in Australia, home of the Opera House

e.etymology: Probably a form of the English surname Ryland, from Old English words for land where rye is grown. As a first name it is recent and follows the sound of Ryan and Dylan.
The Italian form of Angel, from Latin Angelus and Greek angelos, messenger. Italian immigrants made it familiar in the US in the early 1900s.
